title: Woodall’s conjecture
formal: For every finite weakly connected loopless directed multigraph D that is not strongly connected, let \(\tau (D)\) be the minimum size of a directed cut. Must D contain \(\tau (D)\) pairwise arc-disjoint dijoins?
definitions:
A directed multigraph has a finite vertex set V and a finite set A of individually distinguished arcs; parallel arcs are allowed and loops are excluded. Weak connectivity means connectivity after forgetting arc directions. Strong connectivity means that every ordered pair of vertices is joined by a directed path. For \(\varnothing 
e U\subsetneq V\), let \(\delta ^{+}(U)\) be the arcs with tail in U and head outside U, and \(\delta ^{-}(U)\) the arcs entering U. A directed cut, or dicut, is \(\delta ^{+}(U)\) with \(\delta ^{-}(U)=\varnothing\). Under the stated graph assumptions the family of dicuts is nonempty and each dicut has positive size, so \(	au (D)=\min \{|\delta ^{+}(U)|:\varnothing 
e U\subsetneq V, \delta ^{-}(U)=\varnothing\}\) is a finite positive integer. A dijoin is a subset \(J\subseteq A\) meeting every dicut. Pairwise arc-disjoint means \(J_{i}\cap J_{j}=\varnothing\) for \(i
e j\). Every arc has unit capacity; no zero-capacity arcs or other weights are included.
answer_criterion: Prove the existence of \(\tau (D)\) pairwise disjoint dijoins for every stated D, or give a finite D satisfying the assumptions and prove that its maximum packing is smaller than \(\tau (D)\). Since each dijoin must meet a smallest dicut, \(\tau (D)\) is always an upper bound. An approximation by a constant fraction of \(\tau , a\) fractional packing, or a theorem confined to a proper graph subclass is partial progress.

context_blocks.text: A dijoin selects arcs that collectively intercept every one-way boundary of a digraph. Packing dijoins asks how many separate selections can provide this complete coverage without sharing an arc. The smallest one-way boundary is an immediate bottleneck. Woodall’s conjecture says that this visible bottleneck is the only obstruction.

Schrijver lists this exact min–max equality as Survey Question 34. The adjacent Question 33 asks for a polynomial-time algorithm finding a maximum packing. The equality is the structural target here; no efficient construction is demanded as part of a positive answer.

The absence of weights matters. The stronger Edmonds–Giles statement permits arcs of capacity zero as well as one and is false. Deleting a zero-capacity arc can change which sets are dicuts, so it cannot generally turn a weighted counterexample into an unweighted one. The current formulation avoids that false strengthening.

Cornuéjols, Liu and Ravi prove that at least \(\lfloor \tau /6\rfloor\) disjoint dijoins can be constructed in polynomial time. Their argument connects dijoin packing to nowhere-zero flows in the underlying undirected graph. This supplies a constant-factor guarantee while retaining the exact Woodall equality as open.

Weakly disconnected graphs have a zero-size cut and give a trivial zero-packing case. Strongly connected graphs have no dicuts, making the empty set a vacuous dijoin. Restricting the statement to the nontrivial case fixes the meaning of the minimum and maximum without changing the substantive conjecture.

This belongs to combinatorial optimization through the relation between packing and covering, integrality and constructive approximation. It is distinct from a minimum-cost dijoin problem or from maximum directed cut: those optimize different objects, even though some of the vocabulary overlaps.

why: Determine whether the minimum directed-cut capacity exactly characterizes the number of independently usable directed-cut covers, extending the reach of integral packing–covering duality.

importance.reason: A longstanding min–max conjecture in combinatorial optimization, singled out in Schrijver’s survey and the focus of recent approximation and integrality research. The direct packing/covering and algorithmic connections justify inclusion within optimization.

progress.text: Schrijver’s survey lists the exact dijoin-packing equality as Question 34.
The Combinatorica paper proves a polynomial-time \(\lfloor \tau /6\rfloor\) packing guarantee and retains the exact conjecture.

status_note: The unweighted general conjecture remains open in the primary sources checked through 11 September 2026. The false weighted Edmonds–Giles conjecture is a different statement. The checked 2025 constant-factor packing theorem does not imply equality.
review_note: Individually formulated from Schrijver Question 34 and the 2025 primary paper. Explicitly handles cut direction, parallel arcs, unit capacities and degenerate digraphs. No Woodall or dijoin-packing formulation was found in current or archived catalogue records.
